> GOV.UK AI Components — Plain-text agent protocol
> Free to browse and download. Component markup and metadata are original works; GOV.UK class names used under the GOV.UK Design System's terms.
> Home: https://github.com/ednark/govuk-ai-components
> Base layer: https://github.com/ednark/ai-component-registry-spec (submodule at _base/)

---

## Overview

GOV.UK Design System component registry for AI coding agents building UK government services. 41 self-contained component tiles across 29 component families (forms, navigation, feedback, data display, utilities) with categorized adaptation, coordination, and compliance metadata (PSBAR 2018, WCAG 2.2 AA, GDS Service Standard).

## Machine manifest

> https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ednark/govuk-ai-components/main/agents.json

---

## Quick start

1. Filter vocab (tiny): GET https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ednark/govuk-ai-components/main/infinite/facets.json
2. Discovery index (lean): GET https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ednark/govuk-ai-components/main/infinite/components.index.json
3. Component source: GET https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ednark/govuk-ai-components/main/infinite/{file}
4. Recipes (multi-component patterns): GET https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ednark/govuk-ai-components/main/infinite/recipes/index.json
   GOV.UK patterns: ask-users-for-information, check-answers-flow, error-summary-flow,
   task-list-pattern, page-template. When the task matches, fetch the recipe first.
5. Version history: GET https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ednark/govuk-ai-components/main/infinite/versions.json

---

## Facets

- gdsComponentType — button, text-input, checkboxes, radios, date-input, error-summary, notification-banner, accordion, etc.
- section — forms, navigation, feedback, data-display, utilities
- variant — component variant
- interaction — passive, click, focus, keyboard, type, change
- requiresJs — no, optional, required
- govCompliance — PSBAR 2018, WCAG 2.2 AA, GDS Service Standard
- a11y — wcag22AA, keyboardNav, screenReader, reducedMotion, forcedColors, ariaAttributes
- costTier — cheap, moderate, expensive (composition cost: fetch size + JS behavior)
- prerequisites — components to fetch first (e.g., form-group before inputs)
- compositionRecipes — recipes this component participates in
- piiHandling — accepts_input, displays_only, none
- touchTargetSize — guaranteed mobile touch target (44px on interactive components)
- supportedTokenProfiles — token profiles supported (highContrast)

---

## Decision strategy

- GOV.UK deliberately ships no card component — use task-list, summary-list, or heading+link patterns instead of inventing one

1. Filter by section (forms, navigation, feedback, data-display, utilities)
2. Check requiresJs — prefer "no" unless the task needs JS behaviour
3. Verify govCompliance includes PSBAR 2018 / WCAG 2.2 AA
4. Check coordination.prerequisites — fetch form-group before inputs, place error-summary on failed validation
5. Check relatedComponents for commonly paired components
6. Only generate custom UI if no suitable component exists

---

## GOV.UK rules

- One question per page; the question is the label and the h1
- Every input sits inside a govuk-form-group
- Every validation failure shows govuk-error-summary at the top, linked to field errors
- Dates are three separate fields — never add a calendar
- Hints and errors are wired via aria-describedby

---

## Component schema

Each index record: id, file, gdsComponentType, govukClass, title, description, section, variant, variants, requiresJs, interaction, a11y, govCompliance, relatedComponents, costTier, prerequisites, incompatibleWith, compositionRecipes, piiHandling, touchTargetSize, supportedTokenProfiles.

Adaptation prose (useWhen, avoidWhen, agentPrompt, constraints, portability.classMapping.uswds) is embedded in each tile's <script id="govuk-agent-meta"> block — fetch the tile.

---

## Output contract

1. Reason — why this component over alternatives
2. Selected components — file paths and titles
3. GOV.UK classes needed — exact class names to apply
4. Constraint verification — preserve elements intact
5. Remaining work — what the component does not cover
6. Recommended next — what to retrieve next
